To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a method for reconstruct a 3D model of a person's face, from a photo collection, that is robust to the diversity in the number of images, and the image quality.

we present a method for reconstruct a 3D model and albedo from a photo collection of an individual, and that our method is able to adapt to a variety of photo collections with a large diversity in both the image quantity and quality.

(1) we propose a novel photometric-stereo based face reconstruction method that can adapt to unconstrained and diverse photo collections; (2) we propose a coarse-to-finer scheme for face reconstruction; and (3) we propose a new 3D reconstruction quality measure for the case where ground truth 3d scans do not exist.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of 3D face reconstruction from a collection of face images, which is an active area of research.
a practical and scalable solution to reconstruct 3D face models from unconstrained photo collections.
the problem of reconstructing a 2.5D face model (i.e. texture + shape) from unconstrained photo collections of one individual, which can be used for face recognition and 3D face editing applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed approach is able to reconstruct high-quality face models from unconstrained photo collections with high diversity in image quality, number of images and image resolution, and is able to handle a wide range of face poses and expressions.
the method presented in this paper provides a significant improvement over existing methods for 3D face reconstruction from unconstrained photo collections.
the paper presents a novel method for 3D reconstruction of a face from a set of unconstrained images.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed the first approach for reconstructing 3D face models from unconstrained photo collections.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of reconstructing 3D face models of individuals using a small number of images captured under unknown conditions.
, for the first time, it enables the reconstruction of a 3D model of an individual from a small photo collection of “any” individual.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a 3D model can be reconstructed from a small set of unconstrained images, even when the images are captured under a wide range of pose and lighting conditions.
, with a small photo collection, we can achieve a reconstruction quality comparable to state-of-the-art methods with large photo collections.

, given a large enough collection, we can reconstruct a 3D model of a face from a photo collection with a high diversity of pose, expression, lighting, and image quality, without requiring a large photo collection of the individual.
